renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: genotype_grid
  title: HLA class I genotype grid
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample and each column an HLA class I locus (A, B, C); a cell is split in two halves, one per haplotype, coloured by allele group. It answers which alleles every sample carries and which loci are homozygous.
    How to read: alleles of one group share a hue, so a family recurring across the cohort stands out. A merged cell with a marker is a homozygous locus; the side bars give the reads the genotype explains and the solver objective. A sample with few reads deserves a second look before its alleles are used downstream.
    Note: OptiType documents no minimum number of reads for a reliable call, so none is drawn.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FRED-2/OptiType/master/README.md and https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25143287/
  kind: allele_grid
  config:
    allele_group_col: allele_group
    zygosity_col: zygosity
    value_label: Solver objective
    reads_label: Reads explained
  roles:
    sample_id: sample_id
    locus: locus
    allele: allele
    haplotype: haplotype
    category: hla_class
    value: objective
    reads: reads

- component: card
  id: allele_count
  title: Distinct alleles
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct alleles across the samples in view, and the second figure the count of allele calls. The bars rank the loci by distinct alleles. It answers how diverse the cohort is.
    How to read: the locus with the longest bar carries the most alleles in this cohort. A small cohort naturally shows few alleles, so read it with the sample count.
  column: allele
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: locus
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: distinct alleles, by locus
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: homozygous_loci
  title: Homozygous loci
  description: |-
    Each unit is a homozygous locus in a sample, counted once, and the bar splits them by locus. It answers where the cohort loses allelic diversity.
    How to read: homozygosity reduces the peptides a patient can present, so a locus with many homozygous calls matters for epitope prediction. A typing error also looks homozygous when one allele is under-covered, so check the reads in the grid.
  column: locus
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - mode
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: locus
  filter_expr: (col('zygosity') == 'Homozygous') & (col('haplotype') == 1)
  caption: homozygous loci, by locus
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: allele_calls
  title: Allele calls by zygosity
  description: |-
    Each unit is an allele call and the bar shows the share that is homozygous or heterozygous. It answers how often the loci are heterozygous in this cohort.
    How to read: compare the homozygous share with what you expect of the cohort. A high share can be real or a typing artefact, so confirm it against the reads in the grid.
  column: zygosity
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - mode
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: zygosity
  caption: allele calls, by zygosity

- component: figure
  id: allele_frequency
  title: Allele frequency per locus
  description: |-
    Each bar is an allele, with its share of the calls of its locus. It answers which alleles are common in the cohort.
    How to read: a few dominant alleles per locus are typical. The frequencies describe this cohort only, since a small number of samples gives coarse shares.
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: allele
    color: locus
    histnorm: percent
    labels:
      allele: Allele
      locus: Locus

- component: interactive
  title: Allele
  description: Filters the tiles to samples carrying the chosen alleles.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: allele

- component: interactive
  title: Locus
  description: Filters the tiles to one or more HLA class I loci.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: locus

- component: interactive
  title: Zygosity
  description: Filters the tiles to homozygous or heterozygous calls.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: zygosity

- component: table
  title: Allele call table
  description: |-
    Each row is an allele call: one sample, locus and haplotype, with the allele, allele group, zygosity, reads and solver objective. It answers the exact alleles to carry into epitope prediction and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: the allele is spelled as in the epitope prediction tables, so a selected allele matches the same string there.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: call_id

- component: card
  id: typing_reads
  title: Reads explained by the genotype
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of reads that map to the HLA reference and support the chosen genotype, and the box shows the spread. It answers how much evidence each typing rests on.
    How to read: a sample far below the others has little evidence and its alleles are less certain. OptiType documents no minimum number of reads, so judge it against the rest of the cohort.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FRED-2/OptiType/master/README.md
  column: reads
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: reads, quartiles over samples
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: objective_per_read
  title: Objective per read
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median of the solver objective divided by the reads explained, and the box shows the spread. It answers how much of the read evidence the solution keeps at full weight.
    How to read: the ratio is lower by about the homozygosity parameter beta for each heterozygous locus, so it reflects zygosity more than the quality of the fit. Do not read a low value as a bad typing on its own.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FRED-2/OptiType/master/README.md
  column: objective_per_read
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: objective per read, quartiles over samples

- component: card
  id: heterozygous_loci
  title: Heterozygous loci per sample
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of heterozygous loci among the three typed (A, B, C), shown against 3. It answers how heterozygous the cohort is at class I.
    How to read: three means every locus carries two different alleles. Lower values mean homozygous loci, which narrow the set of alleles that can present peptides.
  column: heterozygous_loci
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: gauge
  coverage_max: 3.0
  caption: median out of 3 typed loci

- component: advanced_viz
  id: reads_objective
  title: Solver objective against reads
  description: |-
    Each point is a sample: the reads its genotype explains against the objective value the solver reached, coloured by how many loci are homozygous. It answers whether the objective follows the read support.
    How to read: points lie close to the diagonal, a little below it for each heterozygous locus, so the colour groups follow the zygosity. A point far below its group would be unexpected and worth checking.
    Lines and annotations: the diagonal is the identity, where the objective equals the reads explained. It is a mathematical reference and not a cut-off; OptiType sets the gap with its homozygosity parameter beta.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FRED-2/OptiType/master/README.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Reads explained
    y_title: Solver objective
    reference_line: diagonal
    reference_label: objective equals reads
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    x: reads
    y: objective
    label: sample_id
    color: homozygous_class

- component: figure
  title: Reads per sample
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample and its height the reads that support its genotype, coloured by how many loci are homozygous. It answers which samples carry thin evidence.
    How to read: short bars are samples whose typing rests on few reads. Compare them with the rest of the cohort, as OptiType documents no minimum count.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median number of reads explained of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of OptiType.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample_id
    y: reads
    color: homozygous_class
    labels:
      sample_id: Sample
      reads: Reads explained
      homozygous_class: Homozygous loci
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: reads

- component: table
  title: HLA typing table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its allele pairs at HLA-A, -B and -C, the distinct alleles as a list, zygosity, reads, objective and the runner-up gap. It answers the exact typing to copy into an epitope prediction samplesheet.
    How to read: a runner-up gap near zero means two solutions are almost equally good, so the typing is less certain.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: sample_id
